blocks.x: Midwest University is a private institution of higher education that exists to provide all students with an education designed to prepare them for success in their careers by enhancing their spiritual, social, leadership skills, and intellectual gifts and abilities. With the main campus in the St. Louis metropolitan area city of Wentzville, Missouri, Midwest University offers face-to-face courses, blended courses, and e-learning/distance education opportunities. Midwest University also has offices located in Seoul, South Korea; Lima, Peru; Bangkok, Thailand; and Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam for student advising and student recruitment.

Midwest University is committed to providing students with outstanding learning opportunities in an environment of rigorous academic work, which prepares them for success in their chosen fields of study. The small-class paradigm enhances a personalized learning atmosphere between professors and students.
Midwest University is a member of the following associations:

International Society of Air Safety Investigators (ISASI) - International Council for Distance Education (ICDE) - Council for Adult and Experiential Learning (CAEL) - Association of International Christian Counseling (AICC) - International Evangelical Association (IEA) - Association of Christian Schools International (ACSI) - American Council of Education (ACE) - Association of Christian Higher Education Provider (ACHEP) - Federation of Christian Schools in Korea (FCSK) - International Leadership Association (ILA) - International Education Cooperation (IEC) - ICAO Uniting Aviation

What are you doing to achieve your educational goals? Continuing one's education is necessary for a leader in today's world, regardless of the field he/she is serving in, simply because he/she should be able to envision the future for others. For leadership in the twenty-first century, all relevant education and training acquired to date is insufficient for effective leadership. In today’s world of incessant change, it is imperative to have the responsibility to equip oneself with knowledge, heart, spirit, and leadership. It is essential to cooperate with one another and to share the knowledge students have learned to build team synergy. We are here to challenge the world with educational programs characterized by vision, honesty, and faithfulness, integrity, and responsibility. We need to do our best to develop these characteristics and to build important leadership skills that contribute to the enhancement of our communities, societies, and countries by being valuable lights and salt for the world we live in. God Bless You, Dr. James Song Founder / President

sections.heading: Message from the Board of Trustees Chairman

blocks.x: Midwest University is unique in that it has a distinctly international student body. Midwest University aims to develop knowledgeable students from all around world. During the last several decades, Midwest graduates from around 70 nations have served as experts in their professional areas. Students who are seeking a quality education with a worldview can certainly find a home at Midwest. Our school takes seriously the responsibility to educate people from all over the world. Midwest University is a great resource for students who desire to be well-equipped to apply their learning to teaching and counseling others. Midwest offers programs at Wentzville, MO campus that will provide opportunities for students to develop their God-given gifts and abilities. Students may expand their horizons by taking advantage of both our face-to-face and e-learning classes. If you would like to develop a world vision, I highly encourage you to join Midwest University. I urge you to contact us or visit in-person to find out more about Midwest University. This could be the opportunity you are looking for to develop the next chapter of your academic future. May God Bless You, Dr. Lindell F. Shumake Former MO State Representative Midwest University Board Chairman
Midwest University Foundation Board of trustees

Midwest University exists to provide men and women with a biblically-based higher education designed to prepare them for success in their careers in ministry and secular service by enhancing their spiritual, social, and intellectual gifts and abilities.
Students completing their education at Midwest University will
critique values in view of their understanding of the five areas of general knowledge as appropriate to their degree and evaluate worldview concepts when defining personal values.
engage with university personnel who exhibit integrity in relationships and model a culture that seeks excellence in all that it pursues.
pursue an understanding of God and His will for their lives.
structure their understanding of a profession and formulate strategies for developing an occupation that reflects best practices in the profession.
encounter a wholistic education appropriate to the enrolled students that develops each student spiritually, physically, intellectually, emotionally, and socially.

experience effective teaching from faculty who are qualified academically and experientially to teach in their assigned field and at the assigned education levels, who possess the spiritual and ministerial formation to mentor students toward their desired ministry area, and who are involved appropriately in faculty governance at the institution.
have access to learning resources on campus and online to support their education.

Midwest University acknowledges that all people—regardless of gender, age, or ethnic background—have been given abilities by God and need guidance through education to develop those gifts. Because of this need, Midwest University strives to develop quality educational programs providing systematic and comprehensive academic training from a Christocentric perspective in a curriculum taught by qualified, experienced, and dedicated faculty.
As a distinctly Christian institution of higher education, Midwest University strongly adheres to the principles of:
promotion of the highest academic standards of teaching and learning
respect for the rights of all persons, including the larger global community
commitment to justice, mercy, and caring service
promotion of a true Christian lifestyle

The Bible in its entirety is the inspired Word of God, infallible, sufficient, and authoritative for faith and practice. There is one God, eternally self-existent in three Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. God, through the Word, created the heavens and the earth, and all that is in them for His own good purpose. Jesus Christ, born of a virgin, is God who came in the flesh; His death provides substitutionary atonement for our sins; He rose bodily from the dead and ascended to the right hand of God the Father where He intercedes for the believers. The Holy Spirit indwells believers to enable them to live godly lives and empowers the Church to carry out Christ's Great Commission. The human race was created in the image of God, fell after being tempted by Satan, and because of sinfulness, is inherently in need of salvation found exclusively in Jesus Christ through faith by the power of the Holy Spirit. The one holy Christian Church, the body of Christ, includes all who have come to faith in Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ will return to earth in the Second Advent to judge the living and the dead, to consummate, and to fulfill His purpose in the works of creation and redemption with eternal rewards and punishment.

Founded in 1986 by Dr. James Song, Midwest University is dedicated to discovering and cultivating global talent through excellence in higher education. The University provides academically rigorous and professionally relevant programs that reflect the standards and expectations of American higher education. Guided by a commitment to integrity, scholarship, innovation, and service, Midwest University prepares students to become effective leaders in their professions, communities, and the global arena. The University strives to develop knowledgeable, ethical, and culturally competent graduates who contribute to the advancement of society and the promotion of international understanding and cooperation. The University’s first educational facility was established in 1989. In October 1990, Midwest University began operating as a nonprofit institution of higher education in the State of Missouri, offering degree programs at the bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels. In 1992, Midwest University became a member institution of the Transnational Association of Christian Colleges and Schools (TRACS). In September 1993, the University acquired approximately 17 acres of property in Wentzville, Missouri, to establish its permanent campus. In 1995, the University completed construction of its first major academic building, which included classrooms, a dining facility, and an auditorium. Faculty housing was added in 1996 to support the growing academic community. In 1999, student housing facilities, supporting the University’s long-term campus expansion efforts. In 2000, Midwest University achieved institutional accreditation through TRACS. At that time, TRACS was recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) and the United States Department of Education as an accrediting agency. In 2001, Midwest University received authorization under the Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) to enroll international students and issue Form I-20 for F-1 visa students through SEVIS. In November 2003, the University completed a major administration building that included classrooms, administrative offices, an auditorium, and computer laboratory facilities. Throughout the early 2000s, Midwest University expanded its graduate and doctoral offerings and strengthened its academic infrastructure. In 2005, the institution officially adopted the name Midwest University. In 2006, Midwest University expanded its doctoral offerings, including programs in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL). During the same year, the University received authorization from the U.S. Department of State to participate in the Exchange Visitor Program and to issue Certificates of Eligibility (Form DS-2019) for qualified J-1 Exchange Visitors. On November 3, 2009, Midwest University received a ten-year reaffirmation of accreditation through TRACS. On November 3, 2009, Midwest University received a ten-year reaffirmation of accreditation through TRACS. On November 8, 2011, Midwest University became an institutional member of the Association for Biblical Higher Education (ABHE). On February 18, 2015, the University was granted accredited status through the ABHE Commission on Accreditation. Since 2015, Midwest University has continued to expand its academic offerings through ABHE-approved programs, including business, leadership, aviation, education, counseling psychology, music, computer science, fine arts, and other professional fields. Major academic milestones include: 2015 - Approval of the Master of Business Administration (MBA) Program Exchange Visitor Program Approval from the U.S. Department of State to participate in the Exchange Visitor Program and to issue Certificates of Eligibility (Form DS-2019) for qualified J-1 Exchange Visitors. 2017 - Approval of the Bachelor of Science in Aviation Management, Master of Arts in Gifted Education, Master of Business Administration in Public Policy and Administration, Doctor of Leadership in Brain and Gifted Education, and Doctor of Philosophy in Leadership 2018 - Approval of the Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) 2019 - Approval of the Ph.D. in Counseling Psychology and authorization to participate in the National Council for State Authorization Reciprocity Agreements (NC-SARA), enabling the University to expand distance education opportunities throughout participating states 2020 - Approval of an additional instructional site in Texas 2021 - Ten-Year Reaffirmation of Accreditation by ABHE; approval of an additional instructional site in Irvine, California; and approval of the Ph.D. in Music 2022 - Approval of the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science 2024 - Approval of the Master of Fine Arts (MFA), Doctor of Fine Arts (DFA), Doctor of Business Administration (DBA), Ph.D. in Financial Economics, and Executive Master of Business Administration (EMBA) 2024 - Approval of the Ph.D. Financial Economics 2025 - State of Florida. It is my pleasure to welcome you to the Midwest University ESL Program. It is our intention to provide you with the best possible learning experience during the course of your studies. The English as a Second Language (ESL) Program develops students’ English proficiency for effective communication in the American community and success at the Midwest academic classes that are offered in English. The ESL Program offers its students four proficiency levels of English language studies in the areas of listening and speaking, reading, writing, and grammar. Placement into the appropriate level will be based on a placement exam, an oral interview, and a weeklong study with the instructors. Elective courses are also offered in pronunciation, American culture, current events, TOEFL preparation, and English for ministry. ESL instruction is delivered by degree holding, committed and experienced instructors in classroom settings, and through cultural excursions. The student-teacher ratio is typically about 10:1, providing students with opportunities for individual assistance. We are proud of our program and encourage your inquiries and consideration to join us in at the Midwest University ESL program.

The mission of the English as a Second Language (ESL) program at Midwest University is to give students an opportunity to develop and improve their English proficiency. The multi-level offerings will attempt to enhance student abilities in relaxed, formal, cultural, and academic venues.
Upon completing this certificate program, students will be able to:
Exhibit a broad base of knowledge of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and grammar skills in English.
Successfully adapt to American culture by applying knowledge gained in the classroom.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate with other students and faculty on increasingly sophisticated levels.

Students may achieve twelve (12) transcript notation credits each semester. These credits do not count toward the total number of credits needed to complete an academic program. They also not affect overall GPA.

sections.heading: REQUIREMENTS FOR ADULT DEGREE COMPLETION PROGRAM

blocks.x: This program specifically targets adults who desire to change careers or improve their current educational standing by completing a bachelor’s degree. In particular, the qualifying student will:
Have at least five years of work and/or volunteer experience.

Have completed at least 60 credit hours through prior college/university work with an average 2.0 GPA. Students may enter the program with 45 credit hours but must complete the remaining 15 credit hours before a degree will be granted.
Demonstrate a Christian Commitment.
The Bachelor of Arts in Theology, Business Administration, Bachelor of Science in Aviation and Future Transportation Technology degree programs require 123 semester credit hours to complete.
The student must successfully complete a prescribed course of study with a minimum of 2.00 grade point average (C average) on a 4.00 scale.

Prior to graduation the student must meet all financial obligations to the institution. All candidates for graduation are expected to demonstrate sound scholarship, consistent Christian conduct and attitude, and reasonable suitability for effective Christian ministries. In addition, the appropriate school faculty should fully recommend the candidate for graduation.
All candidates for graduation must complete Christian Service Program and should attend a graduation ceremony.

The Master of Arts in Counseling is designed to equip students for Christian leadership in a local church or para-church organization. This includes training in its foundational courses and courses related to the student’s chosen church-education/leadership concentrations. The Master of Arts in Education is designed to prepare students to serve as educational ministers in a church-based ministry and world mission. The Master of Arts in TESOL is designed to provide students greater opportunities for teaching specialists to enter broader fields of service and to enable them to teach English with the heart of a servant leader. The Master of Business Administration is desire of Midwest University to offer a Masters of Business Administration degree so that students may apply the business knowledge gained from the program in areas of Christian and/or secular services. The Master of Divinity degree is a primary seminary degree for college graduates. This degree requires 96 semester hours to complete in the approved program and it also serves as the basis for doctoral study for those preparing to do research or teach in biblical or theological disciplines. The Master of Music program is designed to train students to serve their local community, church or para-church organization as professional musicians and leaders in their various applied areas. The Master of Fine Arts is dedicated to developing advanced practitioners and educators who can blend artistic prowess with educational strategies.

The Master of Business Administration program is designed to prepare innovative, ethical, and globally competent business leaders who can effectively lead organizations in rapidly changing economic, technological, and international environments. The program emphasizes strategic leadership, entrepreneurship, digital transformation, organizational resilience, global management, and practical decision-making to equip graduates for leadership roles in business, government, healthcare, aviation, public administration, and emerging industries.
Upon completing this degree, students will be able to:
Demonstrate advanced knowledge of business administration, organizational leadership, strategic management, global business, and specialized areas of professional practice.

Apply critical thinking, financial analysis, data analytics, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, and evidence-based decision making to develop innovative solutions for complex organizational and global business challenges.

Demonstrate professional competence through effective leadership, communication, collaboration, entrepreneurship, and strategic decision-making in diverse, multicultural, and technology-driven business environments.

Integrate Christian worldview, ethical leadership, social responsibility, and lifelong learning in leading organizations, serving communities, and promoting sustainable business practices in a global society.
MBA 501 Strategic Leadership and Organizational Management (3)

A comprehensive study of strategic leadership theories, organizational management systems, and executive decision-making within dynamic business environments. The course examines organizational behavior, strategic planning, transformational leadership, team development, conflict management, and organizational change processes. Students develop leadership competencies necessary for managing global organizations, leading innovation initiatives, and improving organizational effectiveness in complex business settings.
MBA 502 Global Business, Economics, and Innovation (3)

An advanced examination of global business systems, international economics, emerging markets, innovation strategy, and competitive business environments. The course explores globalization, international trade, economic policy, global entrepreneurship, digital economies, and innovation-driven organizational growth. Students analyze how technological advancement and global economic trends influence strategic business operations and international management practices.
MBA 503 Digital Transformation, Data Analytics, and Technology Management (3)

A study of digital transformation strategies, business analytics, information systems management, and emerging technologies in modern organizations. The course emphasizes data-driven decision-making, artificial intelligence applications, cloud computing, digital infrastructure, business intelligence systems, and technology integration strategies. Students develop competencies in managing technological innovation and organizational digital transformation.
MBA 504 Business Ethics, Sustainability, and Corporate Governance (3)

An exploration of ethical leadership, sustainability management, environmental and social governance (ESG), corporate responsibility, and governance systems in business organizations. The course examines ethical decision-making models, legal compliance, stakeholder engagement, sustainability strategies, corporate accountability, and responsible leadership practices in global business environments.
MBA 611 AI and Intelligent Business Systems (3)

A comprehensive study of artificial intelligence technologies, intelligent business systems, machine learning applications, and AI-driven organizational operations. Students examine how AI enhances productivity, innovation, customer engagement, operational efficiency, and strategic decision-making across industries and global business environments.
MBA 612 Digital Transformation Strategy (3)

An examination of organizational digital transformation, innovation strategy, digital business models, automation systems, and technology integration frameworks. The course explores how organizations redesign operations, leadership systems, customer experiences, and competitive strategies through digital innovation and emerging technologies.
MBA 613 Global Innovation and Technology Leadership (3)

A study of global innovation ecosystems, technology leadership, strategic innovation management, and digital competitiveness in international business environments. Students analyze innovation-driven organizations, emerging technologies, and leadership strategies that foster creativity, organizational growth, and global market expansion.
MBA 614 AI-Driven Organizational Change (3)

An exploration of AI-enabled organizational transformation, workforce adaptation, intelligent automation, and technology-driven change management. Students examine leadership approaches for managing organizational transition, digital workforce development, innovation culture, and sustainable transformation strategies.
MBA 621 Entrepreneurship and Startup Development (3)

A study of entrepreneurial leadership, startup creation, business opportunity identification, and venture development strategies. Students develop competencies in business model creation, startup planning, market analysis, entrepreneurial finance, and innovation-driven business development.
MBA 622 Venture Strategy and Investment Planning (3)

An examination of venture capital systems, investment planning, startup financing, business valuation, and strategic growth planning for entrepreneurial ventures. The course explores investor relations, funding strategies, financial forecasting, and venture sustainability within competitive business environments.
MBA 623 Innovation Management and Business Creativity (3)

A study of organizational creativity, innovation systems, product development, design thinking, and strategic innovation management. Students analyze methods for fostering innovation culture, improving organizational adaptability, and generating sustainable competitive advantage through creativity and business innovation.
MBA 624 Global Venture Leadership (3)

An exploration of global entrepreneurship, international venture management, cross-cultural business leadership, and global startup ecosystems. Students examine strategies for scaling businesses internationally, leading multicultural teams, and navigating international business expansion and innovation challenges.
MBA 631 AI Marketing Strategy and Consumer Intelligence (3)

This course explores the strategic application of artificial intelligence in modern marketing environments. Students examine how AI technologies - including generative AI, predictive analytics, recommendation engines, and intelligent automation - transform customer acquisition, engagement, and retention. The course emphasizes consumer intelligence, market segmentation, personalization strategies, brand positioning, and AI-supported marketing decision-making. Students analyze real-world business cases and develop AI-driven marketing strategies that improve customer experience and organizational competitiveness.
MBA 632 Customer Analytics and Predictive Marketing (3)

This course develops advanced competencies in customer analytics and data-driven marketing decisions. Students learn methods for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting customer data from CRM systems, digital platforms, social media, and e-commerce environments. Topics include customer segmentation, customer lifetime value (CLV), predictive modeling, behavioral analytics, churn prediction, demand forecasting, and marketing performance measurement. Students utilize business intelligence and AI-powered analytical tools to generate actionable marketing insights and improve organizational performance.
MBA 633 Digital Commerce and Omnichannel Marketing (3)

This course examines digital commerce strategies and integrated omnichannel customer experiences in today’s global marketplace. Students explore e-commerce business models, digital customer journeys, online retail management, mobile commerce, marketplace platforms, digital payment systems, logistics integration, and omnichannel marketing strategies. The course also addresses AI-enabled customer engagement, personalization, digital merchandising, customer relationship management, and conversion optimization. Practical projects enable students to design and evaluate comprehensive digital commerce strategies for domestic and international organizations.
MBA 634 Generative AI, Marketing Automation and Digital Growth (3)

This course focuses on applying generative artificial intelligence and marketing automation technologies to accelerate organizational growth. Students learn how AI-powered platforms support content creation, campaign automation, customer communication, lead generation, email marketing, conversational AI, chatbots, search optimization, social media management, and performance marketing. Additional topics include prompt engineering for marketing professionals, AI ethics, data privacy, responsible AI governance, and marketing ROI optimization. Students complete an applied digital marketing project that integrates AI technologies into a comprehensive marketing growth strategy.
MBA 641 Sustainable Business and ESG Leadership (3)

A study of sustainable business practices, ESG leadership strategies, environmental responsibility, and socially responsible organizational management. Students analyze sustainability frameworks, ethical business operations, and corporate strategies that support long-term organizational and societal impact.
MBA 642 Crisis Management and Organizational Recovery (3)

An examination of crisis leadership, organizational recovery planning, emergency response systems, and crisis communication strategies. Students develop competencies in managing operational disruptions, organizational crises, and recovery initiatives in uncertain business environments.
MBA 643 Risk Management and Business Continuity (3)

A study of enterprise risk assessment, business continuity systems, operational resilience, and organizational risk mitigation strategies. Students analyze financial, technological, operational, and strategic risks affecting organizational sustainability and continuity.
MBA 644 Global Sustainability and Resilient Organizations (3)

An exploration of resilient organizational systems, global sustainability challenges, adaptive leadership, and long-term strategic planning. Students examine how organizations develop resilience, sustainability, and innovation capacity within rapidly changing global environments.
MBA 651 Aviation Management and Operations (3)

A comprehensive study of aviation management systems, airline operations, airport administration, and aviation organizational leadership. Students examine operational planning, aviation logistics, regulatory compliance, and management strategies within global aviation industries.
MBA 652 Aviation Safety and Risk Systems (3)

An examination of aviation safety management systems, operational risk analysis, accident prevention strategies, and aviation regulatory frameworks. Students develop competencies in aviation safety leadership, risk mitigation, and safety culture development.
MBA 653 Airport and Airline Security Management (3)

A study of aviation security systems, airport security operations, airline security protocols, and global transportation security management. Students analyze aviation threat prevention, crisis response, regulatory compliance, and security leadership within aviation environments.
MBA 654 Global Aviation Leadership and Policy (3)

An exploration of international aviation policy, aviation governance systems, global aviation leadership, and strategic management within international aviation organizations. Students examine aviation regulations, international cooperation, and leadership challenges affecting global aviation industries.
MBA 671 Public Administration and Policy Leadership (3)

A study of public-sector leadership, governmental administration, policy implementation, and organizational management within public institutions. Students examine leadership frameworks and strategic governance practices in governmental and nonprofit organizations.
MBA 672 Innovation Strategy in Government Organizations (3)

An examination of innovation systems, digital government transformation, administrative modernization, and organizational innovation strategies within public-sector environments. Students analyze approaches for improving public service efficiency and institutional innovation.
MBA 673 Global Public Policy and Governance (3)

A study of global governance systems, international policy development, public administration models, and comparative governmental leadership practices. Students examine policy analysis and governance challenges within international and multicultural environments.
MB 674 Strategic Leadership in Public Institutions (3)

An exploration of strategic leadership, organizational change, crisis governance, and decision-making within governmental agencies and public institutions. Students develop competencies for leading complex public-sector organizations effectively.

sections.heading: 7. Real Estate Investment Management and Auction

blocks.x: MBA 681 Real Estate Investment and Asset Management (3)

A comprehensive study of real estate investment strategies, asset management systems, property valuation, and portfolio development. Students analyze investment opportunities, market performance, and strategic property management practices.
MBA 682 Property Development and Market Analysis (3)

An examination of property development processes, market feasibility analysis, urban development trends, and real estate project planning. Students evaluate real estate market conditions and development strategies for commercial and residential projects.
MBA 683 Real Estate Finance and Portfolio Strategy (3)

A study of real estate financing systems, mortgage structures, investment portfolio management, and financial analysis within property markets. Students develop competencies in evaluating financial performance and managing real estate investment portfolios.
MBA 684 Auction Systems and Investment Negotiation (3)

An exploration of auction systems, investment negotiation strategies, bidding processes, and transactional leadership within real estate and asset markets. Students examine negotiation techniques and strategic acquisition methods in competitive investment environments.
MBA 691 Health Care Leadership and Organizational Effectiveness (3)

This course examines leadership theories, organizational behavior, and management practices within health care organizations. Students develop competencies in strategic leadership, organizational culture, ethical decision-making, workforce development, team leadership, and organizational effectiveness. Emphasis is placed on leading hospitals, clinics, senior care organizations, home health agencies, and community health services in rapidly changing environments.
MBA 692 Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Health Care (3)

This course explores innovation, entrepreneurship, and new business development in the health care industry. Students examine emerging health care markets, business model innovation, health care startups, senior care enterprises, home health services, and strategic growth opportunities. Topics include business planning, financial sustainability, innovation management, and entrepreneurial leadership.
MBA 693 Digital Health and AI Applications in Health Care (3)

This course introduces digital transformation and artificial intelligence applications in modern health care systems. Students explore electronic health records, telehealth, digital health platforms, health analytics, AI-assisted decision support, cybersecurity, and technology- driven operational improvements. The course emphasizes innovation and data-informed leadership for improving patient care and organizational performance.
MBA 694 Strategic Health Care Operations and Quality Improvement (3)

This course focuses on strategic operations management, quality improvement, regulatory compliance, patient safety, and performance excellence in health care organizations. Students learn methods for improving operational efficiency, financial performance, accreditation readiness, risk management, and continuous quality improvement across diverse health care settings.
MBA 711 Strategic Business Management (3)

A comprehensive study of strategic business management principles, organizational competitiveness, operational leadership, and executive decision-making within modern business environments. The course examines strategic planning, organizational alignment, performance improvement systems, competitive analysis, and leadership strategies that support sustainable business growth and organizational effectiveness.
MBA 712 Marketing Strategy and Consumer Engagement (3)

An examination of modern marketing systems, consumer behavior, customer engagement strategies, and integrated marketing communication within competitive global markets. The course explores branding, market positioning, customer relationship management, digital marketing integration, and data-informed marketing strategies that improve organizational visibility and customer loyalty.
MBA 713 Organizational Leadership and Business Communication (3)

A study of organizational leadership, executive communication, team management, negotiation strategies, and interpersonal leadership systems in business organizations. The course focuses on leadership communication, organizational culture, conflict management, collaborative leadership, and professional relationship development necessary for effective organizational performance.
MBA 714 Innovation, Business Growth, and Market Expansion (3)

An exploration of innovation strategy, business growth systems, market expansion planning, and entrepreneurial business development. The course examines innovation-driven competitiveness, product and service development, emerging market opportunities, business scalability, and strategic growth leadership within dynamic business environments.
MBA 715 Data Science for Business Decision-Making (3)

This course introduces the principles and applications of data science in modern business organizations. Students examine data collection, data management, descriptive analytics, predictive modeling, and business intelligence techniques used to support managerial decision- making. Emphasis is placed on transforming organizational data into actionable insights that improve strategic planning, operational performance, and competitive advantage.
MBA 716 Business Analytics & Predictive Intelligence (3)

This course explores advanced business analytics tools and predictive intelligence for solving organizational challenges. Students study descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics, forecasting techniques, key performance indicators (KPIs), executive dashboards, and data visualization methods. The course emphasizes applying analytical models to improve organizational effectiveness, customer engagement, financial performance, and strategic decision-making.
MBA 717 Enterprise Data Management & Digital Strategy (3)

This course examines enterprise data management and digital strategy from a managerial perspective. Students explore information systems, data governance, cloud computing, cybersecurity fundamentals, business intelligence platforms, enterprise analytics, and digital transformation strategies. Emphasis is placed on aligning organizational data assets and emerging technologies with business objectives, innovation, and sustainable growth.
MBA 718 Artificial Intelligence & Business Intelligence (3)

This course examines the application of artificial intelligence and business intelligence technologies in organizational leadership and business strategy. Students explore machine learning concepts, generative AI, intelligent automation, executive analytics, AI-assisted decision support, and responsible AI practices. Emphasis is placed on leveraging AI-driven technologies to enhance organizational performance, innovation, customer value, and executive decision-making.

The program is dedicated to developing advanced practitioners and educators who can blend artistic prowess with educational strategies. The program aims to foster a symbiotic relationship between creative practice and educational theory, positioning art as both a personal expressive medium and a tool for societal transformation. Also, it seeks to imbue students with a biblical worldview, integrating biblical engagement and theological reflection into the fabric of their artistic and educational endeavors.
Upon completing this degree, students will be able to:
Skill Enhancement: To enhance students' artistic skills and broaden their perspectives across various art forms, grounded in a biblical worldview.

Cultivation of Inclusive Educators: To prepare educators who integrate diverse cultural perspectives and inclusive methodologies into their teaching, while embedding biblical principles and theological insights.
Understanding Art's Therapeutic Potential: To deepen understanding of art's therapeutic capabilities for well-being, emphasizing how biblical perspectives can enhance therapeutic practices.

Integration of Technology: To equip students with skills to integrate digital technologies in art education, exploring how these technologies can be used to further biblical engagement and reflection.

Promotion of Critical Engagement: To encourage critical engagement with contemporary art and education issues, advocating for art's role in society and its capacity to convey and reflect biblical truths.

The program believes in art's transformative power, emphasizing a holistic approach that integrates theory, practice, and societal involvement. It views the artist-educator as an agent of change, deeply rooted in a biblical framework that guides personal expression and professional practice.

The MFA program offers a rich curriculum designed to advance skills and knowledge in art and education, preparing students for leadership in the arts. The curriculum is uniquely crafted to include biblical engagement and theological reflection as core components, ensuring that graduates are well-equipped to apply their artistic skills within a framework that supports spiritual and societal transformation.

The Doctor of Leadership degree empowers students with the skills needed to bring about higher performance levels within their organization as they learn about the dynamics of promoting effective leadership development, interpersonal relationships, and group and organizational dynamics. The Doctor of Business Administration program is designed to provide students with advanced knowledge and skills in business administration, strategic management, and leadership, all within a framework grounded in Christian values. The Doctor of Ministry degree is a professional degree which is designed for those engaged in pastoral ministries or other areas of Christian service. The doctoral curriculum provides students with an opportunity to select one of the four suggested vocational emphasis. The Doctor of Musical Arts is to equip students with superior academic excellence emphasizing intensive musical techniques and research in music literatures in their applied area, and also train students to make positive global impact as dynamic music leaders by advancing their performance techniques and profound musical knowledge preparing artists for careers in higher education. The Doctor of Philosophy in Counseling Psychology is designed to prepare students for leadership roles of the field in the areas of advanced clinical counseling practice, advanced research and supervision. The degree of Doctor of Philosophy allows students to pursue Marriage and Family Counseling, Mental Health Counseling, and Life Design Counseling and Coaching. Additionally, the degree will be awarded upon the student's demonstration of a broad understanding of certain fields of knowledge, ability to conduct independent research, and ability to organize research into an acceptable dissertation that will represent a contribution to a field of study. The Doctor of Philosophy in Education is designed to help students to be equipped with a higher level of teaching and research capabilities. This program provides more advanced leadership in education including teaching and learning, research and practice, curriculum analysis and development, other teaching in higher education, and leadership positions in educational agencies. Furthermore, this program enables students to apply their scholastic knowledge in their educational field. The Doctor of Philosophy in Leadership is designed to help students to be equipped with a higher level of teaching and research capabilities in leadership. This program provides more advanced leadership training in the fields of ministry, adult and brain & gifted education, politics, and business. Furthermore, this program enables students to apply their scholastic knowledge in their educational, governmental, business, and pastoral organizations. The Ph.D. program in Financial Economics is designed to develop scholars and researchers capable of advancing knowledge in the field of financial economics. The Integrated Master’s and Doctoral Program is designed for highly qualified students who wish to pursue advanced graduate studies leading directly to the doctoral degree. Students are admitted into the Doctoral program from the beginning and may earn a master’s degree en route to the Doctor degree upon successful completion of the required coursework and research milestones. This structure allows for a streamlined progression of studies, combining rigorous master’s-level foundations with advanced doctoral research, while reducing the total time to degree completion. Midwest University offers such Integrated Master’s and Doctoral Programs in each major field of study.

The DFA program at Midwest University is designed to elevate artists, researchers, and leaders in the fine arts by achieving the following purposes:
Cultivate Advanced Artistic Skills: Enhancing high-level proficiency across art forms to push creative boundaries.
Foster Innovative Research in Fine Arts: Stimulating original research that blends traditional techniques with contemporary practices, expanding the arts.
Prepare Leaders in the Arts Community: Developing leadership and entrepreneurial skills for significant impact on the art world, locally and globally.
Upon completing this degree, students will be able to:
Mastery of Artistic Mediums: Students will achieve advanced mastery in their chosen medium, producing impactful work.
Professional Development: Acquisition of skills for collegiate teaching, professional exhibiting, and artistic collaboration.
Global and Cultural Awareness: Understanding the global and cultural contexts of art, appreciating diversity in artistic expression.
The DFA program is built on four foundational pillars:
Interdisciplinary Approach: Valuing interdisciplinary collaboration to foster a comprehensive understanding of the arts.
Commitment to Innovation: Promoting a culture where experimentation and innovation in fine arts are encouraged.
Ethical Artistic Practice: Advocating for integrity, responsibility, and respect for diverse perspectives in artistic creation.
Community Engagement: Emphasizing art's role in communication, social change, and cultural enrichment within communities.

The DFA curriculum is meticulously designed to offer a blend of advanced artistic training, rigorous research, and leadership development tailored for the arts community. With an emphasis on both the mastery of specific artistic mediums and the exploration of new artistic horizons, the program prepares students for a range of roles, including university teaching positions, professional artists, and community arts leaders. Students will complete a mix of studio work, scholarly research, and practical applications of their studies, culminating in a significant final project or dissertation that demonstrates their contribution to the field of fine arts. Through this comprehensive approach, the DFA program aims to produce well-rounded professionals equipped to influence and innovate within the dynamic landscape of the arts.

The program seeks to cultivate visionary leaders capable of integrating research, technology, and global business strategies for organizational excellence and societal impact.

The course examines environmental stewardship, ethical governance, social responsibility, and sustainable business practices that contribute to long-term organizational value. Students develop sustainability-driven leadership strategies for future-focused organizations.
DBA 832 Crisis Leadership and Organizational Resilience (4)

An examination of crisis management systems, organizational resilience frameworks, and executive leadership strategies during emergencies and disruptions. The course explores crisis communication, decision-making under uncertainty, disaster response, and organizational recovery planning. Students develop leadership competencies for managing complex organizational crises effectively.
DBA 833 Climate Risk, Energy Transition, and Future Sustainability (4)

A study of climate risk management, renewable energy systems, carbon reduction strategies, and future sustainability. The course examines operational risk, financial risk, security threats, and emergency preparedness strategies essential for organizational stability and resilience. Students learn to design comprehensive risk management and recovery frameworks.
DBA 834 Sustainable Innovation and Circular Economy Leadership (4)

An examination of circular economy systems, sustainable innovation, green technologies, ESG transformation. and future enterprise leadership. The course examines global sustainability initiatives, environmental policy trends, and long-term development strategies affecting organizational leadership. Students analyze future-oriented solutions for sustainable business growth.
DBA 835 Strategic Crisis Communication and Stakeholder Engagement (4)

A study of crisis communication systems, public trust management, organizational reputation, recovery leadership strategies, and stakeholder management during organizational emergencies. The course examines media relations, public communication, organizational reputation management, and post-crisis recovery planning. Students develop executive communication competencies for crisis response and organizational stabilization.
DBA 836 Global Risk Management and Business Continuity (4)

An exploration of global security systems, organizational continuity planning, and strategic resilience management within complex business environments. The course focuses on geopolitical risk, cyber threats, operational security, and continuity leadership strategies that support organizational sustainability. Students evaluate integrated approaches to long-term organizational protection and resilience.
DBA 841 Aviation Systems and Global Operations (4)

A study of aviation systems, global aviation operations, and strategic management within international aviation industries. The course examines airline operations, airport systems, aviation logistics, and global aviation infrastructure influencing operational efficiency and organizational leadership. Students explore strategic management practices in modern aviation environments.
DBA 842 Aviation Safety and Security Leadership (4)

An examination of aviation safety systems, aviation security management, and regulatory compliance in domestic and international aviation sectors. The course focuses on risk reduction, accident prevention, crisis response, and leadership strategies that enhance aviation safety performance. Students develop competencies in aviation safety leadership and security administration.
DBA 843 Airport and Airline Strategic Management (4)

A study of airport operations, airline administration, and strategic aviation leadership in competitive global markets. The course explores aviation policy, financial management, operational planning, and customer service systems within airport and airline organizations. Students evaluate management strategies for sustainable aviation growth and operational excellence.
DBA 844 Future Aviation Technology and Innovation (4)

An exploration of emerging aviation technologies, smart transportation systems, and innovation trends shaping the future of global aviation. The course examines unmanned aerial systems, AI-based aviation systems, advanced mobility technologies, and future transportation infrastructure. Students analyze technological innovation and strategic leadership opportunities within evolving aviation industries.
DBA 845 Aviation Crisis and Emergency Management (4)

A study of aviation emergency systems, crisis response strategies, and operational recovery management within aviation organizations. The course examines aviation disasters, emergency coordination, safety protocols, and executive leadership practices that support operational continuity. Students develop competencies for managing complex aviation emergencies and crisis situations.
DBA 846 Global Aviation Policy and Regulatory Leadership (4)

An exploration of international aviation regulations, aviation policy systems, and global leadership challenges affecting modern aviation industries. The course focuses on ICAO standards, regulatory compliance, international aviation governance, and strategic policy leadership. Students analyze global regulatory frameworks and aviation leadership strategies within international markets.
DBA 851 Global Maestro Leadership and Human Development (4)

A study of transformational leadership development, human-centered organizational management, and executive leadership effectiveness in global environments. The course examines emotional intelligence, leadership psychology, organizational behavior, and strategic human development systems. Students develop advanced leadership competencies for international organizational settings.
DBA 852 Organizational Communication and Global Influence (4)

An examination of organizational communication strategies, executive influence systems, and leadership interaction within global organizations. The course explores communication dynamics, negotiation strategies, intercultural leadership, and influence management in diverse organizational environments. Students strengthen leadership communication skills for international management and executive leadership.
DBA 853 Talent Development and Executive Coaching (4)

A study of talent management systems, executive coaching models, and leadership mentoring strategies in organizational settings. The course focuses on leadership assessment, employee development, performance coaching, and succession planning for sustainable organizational growth. Students learn practical coaching methodologies for executive and organizational development.
DBA 854 Global Organizational Excellence and Innovation (4)

An exploration of organizational excellence models, innovation systems, and strategic leadership practices that improve global organizational performance. The course examines quality management, organizational transformation, operational effectiveness, and innovation-driven leadership systems. Students develop strategic frameworks for achieving organizational excellence in international environments.
DBA 855 Human Capital Strategy and Leadership Psychology (4)

A study of human capital development strategies, leadership psychology, and workforce performance systems within global organizations. The course examines motivation theory, leadership behavior, organizational culture, and psychological frameworks influencing executive leadership effectiveness. Students develop strategic approaches for enhancing organizational human performance.
DBA 856 Cross-Cultural Leadership and Global Team Management (4)

An examination of cross-cultural leadership systems, global workforce management, and international organizational collaboration strategies. The course explores cultural intelligence, global communication, team leadership, and organizational adaptability in multinational environments. Students strengthen competencies for leading culturally diverse organizations and global teams.

sections.heading: 6. Real Estate Investment Management and Auction

blocks.x: DBA 861 Real Estate Investment and Asset Management (4)

A study of real estate investment strategies, asset portfolio management, and property valuation systems in domestic and international markets. The course examines investment analysis, real estate finance, portfolio diversification, and strategic asset management for long-term financial growth. Students evaluate investment opportunities and risk management strategies in real estate markets.
DBA 862 Property Development and Market Analysis (4)

An examination of property development processes, market analysis methodologies, and strategic planning within real estate industries. The course focuses on land development, feasibility studies, market forecasting, and investment evaluation in commercial and residential real estate sectors. Students develop analytical competencies for successful property development projects.
DBA 863 Auction Theory and Real Estate Transactions (4)

A study of auction systems, negotiation strategies, and transactional management in real estate industries. The course examines auction theory, bidding systems, legal procedures, and strategic negotiation practices related to property transactions. Students develop practical knowledge of real estate transaction management and auction-based investment systems.
DBA 864 Global Real Estate Strategy and Finance (4)

An exploration of international real estate systems, global investment strategies, and financial management within real estate industries. The course examines cross-border investment, global property markets, financing structures, and international development strategies affecting real estate organizations. Students evaluate global trends and financial opportunities in real estate investment.
DBA 865 Commercial Real Estate and Urban (4)

A study of commercial real estate systems, urban development planning, and strategic investment management in metropolitan environments. The course examines urban economics, commercial property development, infrastructure investment, and city growth strategies influencing real estate markets. Students analyze sustainable urban development and commercial investment opportunities.
DBA 866 Global Property Investment and Wealth Strategy (4)

An exploration of global property investment systems, wealth management strategies, and international real estate portfolio development. The course focuses on investment diversification, international financing, tax considerations, and long-term asset growth strategies within global real estate markets. Students evaluate wealth-building opportunities and strategic investment frameworks.
DBA 871 Health Care Leadership and Administration (4)

A study of leadership principles, administrative systems, and organizational management practices within health care institutions. The course examines health care leadership models, organizational structure, human resource management, and operational effectiveness in hospitals and medical organizations. Students develop executive competencies for health care administration and organizational leadership.
DBA 872 Health Care Policy and Strategic Planning (4)

An examination of health care systems, policy development, and strategic planning processes within public and private health care organizations. The course focuses on policy analysis, regulatory systems, health care reform, and organizational strategy affecting health care delivery and management. Students evaluate policy frameworks and strategic solutions for health care leadership.
DBA 873 Health Care Operations and Quality Management (4)

A study of operational systems, quality assurance practices, and organizational performance improvement in health care settings. The course examines patient care systems, operational efficiency, accreditation standards, and quality management strategies that improve organizational effectiveness. Students develop leadership skills for managing health care operations and performance systems.
DBA 874 Innovation and Technology in Health Care Systems (4)

An exploration of digital health technologies, innovation systems, and emerging medical technologies transforming health care organizations. The course examines telemedicine, electronic health systems, AI applications in medicine, and technology-driven patient care strategies. Students analyze future trends and innovation opportunities in health care leadership and administration.
DBA 875 Global Public Health and Health Care Leadership (4)

A study of global public health systems, international health care leadership, and strategic management practices affecting population health. The course examines health disparities, global health policy, crisis response systems, and leadership strategies within international health care environments. Students evaluate global health challenges and organizational leadership solutions.
DBA 876 Health Care Innovation, Ethics, and Future Systems (4)

An exploration of innovation leadership, ethical decision-making, and future-oriented health care systems within evolving medical environments. The course focuses on AI in health care, biotechnology innovation, ethical governance, and strategic transformation in modern medical organizations. Students analyze emerging trends and future leadership opportunities in health care industries.
DBA 881 Advanced Data Science Foundations (4)

Provides an advanced study of data science principles, statistical reasoning, data preparation, analytical frameworks, and data-driven decision-making for executive leadership. Students learn how organizations transform data into strategic business intelligence.
DBA 882 Machine Learning for Business Intelligence (4)

Explores supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques, predictive analytics, classification, clustering, neural networks, and AI applications that support business innovation and executive decision-making.
DBA 883 Artificial Intelligence for Strategic Decision Making (4)

Examines the application of artificial intelligence, generative AI, intelligent decision support systems, automation technologies, and AI-driven business transformation for organizational leadership and competitive advantage.
DBA 884 Data Governance, Privacy, and Ethical Leadership (4)

Studies enterprise data governance, cybersecurity awareness, information privacy, regulatory compliance, responsible AI, and ethical leadership necessary for managing data-driven organizations in a global environment.
DBA 885 Digital Transformation and Intelligent Enterprise Systems (4)

Focuses on digital transformation strategies integrating AI, business analytics, cloud technologies, enterprise systems, intelligent automation, and innovation management to improve organizational performance and long-term sustainability.

sections.heading: (Students may select either Option A or Option B)
(Each course carries 1 credit hour. Students complete a total of 8 courses.)

blocks.x: DBA 891 Doctoral Business Practicum I (1)

An introductory doctoral practicum designed to provide supervised professional experience in business leadership, organizational operations, and applied management practices. Students engage in practical observation, leadership participation, and reflective analysis within professional organizational settings.
DBA 892 Doctoral Business Practicum II (1)

A continuation of supervised doctoral practicum experiences emphasizing advanced organizational engagement, leadership application, and strategic business problem-solving. Students demonstrate increasing professional competency through applied executive-level responsibilities.
DBA 893 Applied Organizational Leadership Practicum (1)

An applied practicum focused on leadership development, organizational effectiveness, and executive communication within complex organizational environments. Students examine practical leadership strategies and organizational behavior through supervised field engagement.
DBA 894 Advanced Business Strategy Field Experience (1)

A field-based experiential course designed to strengthen strategic management competencies through direct exposure to executive planning, competitive analysis, organizational innovation, and strategic implementation practices within business organizations.
DBA 895 Management Internship I(1)

A supervised management internship providing practical experience in business administration, operational management, and organizational leadership. Students apply doctoral-level knowledge to real-world business and institutional environments.
DBA 896 Management Internship II (1)
An advanced internship emphasizing executive leadership, organizational development, strategic decision-making, and professional management practices in global and multicultural business settings.
DBA 897 Global Business Leadership Practicum (1)

An experiential practicum examining global leadership competencies, international business communication, cross-cultural management, and global organizational strategy. Students develop leadership skills for international business environments.
DBA 898 Doctoral Applied Business Consulting Project (1)

A doctoral-level consulting practicum in which students analyze organizational challenges, develop strategic recommendations, and present evidence-based business solutions for institutional or corporate clients through supervised consulting projects.

sections.heading: Option B: Independent Research / Study Track
(In place of the practicum track, students may choose 8 credit hours of Free Elective courses.)

blocks.x: RS 805 Dissertation Research Seminar (3)

This course provides doctoral students with comprehensive guidance in the development, design, and completion of dissertation research. Students will explore advanced research methodologies, academic writing standards, literature review strategies, data collection and analysis procedures, and ethical considerations in scholarly research. Emphasis is placed on developing a well-structured dissertation proposal, conducting independent research, and preparing scholarly work suitable for doctoral-level academic and professional contribution. The seminar also supports students through the stages of dissertation planning, organization, presentation, and final defense preparation.
RS 807 Dissertation (6)

A minimum of 100 pages is required for dissertations. The title of the dissertation and the subject matter to be covered must be presented to the selected Chairman of the Student's Dissertation Committee for approval prior to beginning the research project.
CP 890 Capstone (3)

The Capstone course is designed as a final semester summative course for students to exhibit how their educational experience may positively influence their career. Details will be described in the Capstone syllabus. The Capstone will have three sections: 1) a research project agreed upon with their academic advisors prior to the final semester 2) a comprehensive examination 3) participation in the graduation seminars.

The Service Leadership Engagement Program is designed to cultivate servant leadership, ethical responsibility, professional integrity, and community engagement through structured leadership service activities. Doctoral students participate in community service, organizational leadership projects, and professional engagement experiences that strengthen ethical leadership and social responsibility competencies.
Option 1 - Community Service
Complete 24 hours of approved community service, demonstrating leadership, civic engagement, and service to the community.
Option 2 - Leadership Service Seminar

Complete a 1-credit Leadership Service Seminar, which focuses on the role and responsibilities of leaders in serving communities. Students are required to attend the seminar and successfully complete a reflective report or assigned project demonstrating their understanding and application of service leadership principles.

sections.heading: Doctor of Philosophy in Financial Economics

blocks.x: The Ph.D. program in Financial Economics is designed to develop scholars and researchers capable of advancing knowledge in the field of financial economics. The program aims to equip students with a deep understanding of financial theories, empirical methods, and advanced analytical tools, all within the financial framework. Graduates will be prepared for careers in academia, research institutions, and high-level policy-making positions, where they can apply their expertise to influence financial practices in ways that reflect integrity, stewardship, and ethical responsibility as taught in the Biblical principles.
Upon completing this degree, students will be able to:

Develop advanced knowledge and understanding of the core principles and advanced concepts in financial economics, including financial theory, investment analysis, international finance, and financial markets.
Foster a global perspective on financial economics, recognizing the interconnectedness of global financial markets and the importance of international financial policies and practices.

Specialized Expertise: Offer specialized training in various emphasis areas such as financial economics, investment and financial management, corporate finance and investment, and finance and accounting. Students are encouraged to tailor their studies to their research interests and career goals, while also considering how their work can serve broader societal needs in line with biblical teachings on service and stewardship.
Have a strong sense of ethical responsibility and professional standards and apply biblical principles such as honesty, fairness, and respect for others in their professional conduct.
Application form for admission
$100.00 non-refundable application fee
A brief autobiographical statement

Applicant Qualifications : 1) Master's degree holder (Every major) 2) To enter the Ph.D. program in Finance, students must have majored in Finance in their master program. If they did not major in Finance, they must take 12~24 additional credits as prerequisite courses. 3) The completed course with grade C+ below would not be counted as credit hours. 4) GPA should be above 3.5

Admission Procedures : Admission procedures consist of application screening, entrance exam, and interview. 1) Applicants should pass application screening before taking entrance tests. Application includes applicant's essay, recommendation letters, and transcripts. 2) The test areas are essay and English (reading). 3) Program faculities will interview applicants who take tests. 4) Application screening, written essay test, English test and interview respectively take up 100 points (Total 400 points). Admission would be given to the applicants who scored 320 points above. 5) Faculty committee will make all admission decisions.
Two recent photographs (for student ID)
The Doctoral Program is designed to be completed within five academic years. A maximum of seven years may be granted upon appeal to the Academic Dean.
The student must successfully complete a prescribed course of study with a minimum of 3.00 (B) grade point average on a 4.00 scale.
The awarding of a “C” in a doctoral course constitutes a failure (unsuccessful completion of the course).
The student must pass a qualifying examination.
The student must successfully complete a dissertation and pass the oral defense.
Prior to graduation the student must meet all financial obligations to the institution.
All candidates for graduation must complete a non-credit course, GE 500 Worldview. It will be waived for the students who have taken any biblical courses.
